Meta Ad Library census · refreshed 27 Aug 2026

Persona Census

The longest-running live ads from 120 tracked competitors across ten DTC categories — each read for who it casts and what it needs them to believe. Harvested straight from Meta's Ad Library, so there is no spend and no impressions here: the ranking metric is survival.

How this is built

Meta's Ad Library pagination query is replayed for each advertiser, filtered to ads whose start date precedes a descending ladder of cutoffs. Everything surviving a restrictive cutoff is by definition that brand's set of longest runners — so the picks are provably the oldest, not a sample.

Creatives are deduplicated on CDN content id, then clustered by concept (landing path + copy fingerprint), so each brand's cards are different arguments rather than re-uploads of one.

What days-running is not

The Ad Library exposes no impressions and no spend for US commercial ads, so nothing here is a performance ranking. Days-running measures competitor conviction — how long a team has kept paying for something — which is a survival proxy, not a return.

Cadence differs by more than 25× across these advertisers, so longevity is only comparable within a brand, never across the table.

Coverage & gaps

141 ads carry a hand-written read; 362 carry a provisional keyword tag and 137 are unread. Filter to Hand-read below to see only the reviewed set.

No live US ads: Your Heights, Matcha Fuel, OYL Mushroom Coffee, The Sleep Company, SleepyCat, STIHL +1 more.

Port structure, never claim language. Several brands here run claims that would not clear another advertiser's compliance review. The mechanics travel; the copy does not.

What repeats across the set

Patterns visible only once the personas are named

Hormones are the universal villain — for both sexes

Cortisol, testosterone and peri-menopause do identical work across the set: they move the cause of a body the buyer dislikes from their behaviour to their biology. Happy Mammoth's 5 signs cortisol is controlling your body, Primal Queen's you're not broken … it's peri-menopause and Mars Men's no beer? no problem, cortisol's got your belly covered are one psychographic in three costumes: it isn't my fault, and the mechanism has a name.

GLP-1 is generating personas, not just demand

Four brands address four different people created by the same drug. Huel sells to the patient whose appetite vanished; Grüns to the one with constipation and sulfur burps; Primal Queen sells PQ7 as no injections, no jitters; Mars Men catches the man at before you start injections. Companion, side-effect fixer and refusenik are three separate buyers — treating GLP-1 as one audience leaves two of them unserved.

The heaviest spenders run the fewest ideas

RYZE keeps 80 distinct creatives alive that express only 3 concepts. Lineage runs 31 for 3. Flamingo runs 30 for 2. Volume advertisers vary the asset, never the argument — which is why their copy is useless for identifying a format and the composition has to be read instead. Watch the creatives→concepts column: a tight ratio marks a brand running a machine, not a test.

Medical-authority cosplay is the default proof device

Lab coats at Primal Queen and Resilia, Doctor Reacts at Ulike, from a real cancer researcher at Resilia, made by Yale-educated scientists at Thesis, and Primal Viking's my doctor told me something he'd never told a patient before. In none of these is the clinician the advertiser's own. The persona being served distrusts their actual doctor and trusts a credentialed dissenter.

Apology as an offer mechanic

We Made Too Much (Primal Viking), We really fcked up this time (Hismile), Apologies to last week's buyers (Mars Men), We're sorry — here's 55% off (Paleovalley). Framing the discount as a mistake or a logistics failure lets the price drop without conceding the product was ever worth less.

At the premium end, risk reversal replaced the discount

RŌZ's longest-running structure is a checkout screen reading Due Today $0.00 — only pay if your hair loves it. Norse Organics converts its returns policy into the efficacy claim: our return policy is simple. Acne will never return. Where price is the objection, the winning offer is don't pay yet, not pay less.
